title: BANXUM P2P Primer: what you need to know before you touch a screen

sections.heading: 1. What BANXUM is
body: BANXUM is a peer-to-peer (P2P) lending marketplace. "Peer-to-peer" means individual people lend money directly to businesses, instead of a bank sitting in the middle and lending its own money.

Here is the basic idea. Individual investors (we also call them "lenders") put money into BANXUM. That money is then used to fund loans to vetted business borrowers. The borrowers pay the money back over time, with interest. The interest is shared back to the investors who funded that loan. Investors can later take their money out again.

BANXUM is operated by Garanta Finanzgruppe AG, a Swiss financial group. "Garanta" is the operator, and you, as an operations admin, work for Garanta. BANXUM does not lend its own money and is not a bank. It runs the marketplace, checks who everyone is, moves money correctly, and keeps records.

This manual is about the internal ops console served at /admin, which only Garanta staff use. It is NOT the app that investors log into. Throughout this manual, "the console" or "the admin console" always means the staff tool, never the investor app.

sections.heading: 2. The four people in the story
body: Almost everything in BANXUM involves these four parties. Learn them first; the rest of the manual refers to them constantly.
bullets: Investor (lender): an individual who deposits money and funds loans to earn interest. In the system an investor account has an account_type of either "natural_person_lender" (a real human investing for themselves) or "legal_entity_lender_representative" (a person acting on behalf of a company that invests). Every lender account is given a short unique investor_reference code when it is created. Investors log into the investor app themselves; they do not use the admin console.

Borrower: a company that receives a loan and pays it back with interest. A borrower is NEVER a login account. It is a record (a "BorrowerEntity") that you, the admin, create and maintain by hand. The borrower has no portal, no password, and never logs in anywhere. Borrowers are vetted through KYB (explained in section 7) before they can receive money.

Garanta operator (you): a Garanta staff member working in the admin console. There are two staff account types: "admin" (normal operations staff) and "superadmin" (staff who can also change platform-wide settings and create other admins). Note that the account type alone is not enough: admin powers also depend on the account's is_staff flag being set, and superadmin powers additionally require the is_superuser flag, so a "superadmin" account type that lacks is_superuser would not pass superadmin checks. You enter borrowers and loans, review compliance, confirm bank movements, and run the day-to-day operation.

Didit: an external identity-verification company. "External" means it is a third-party provider, not part of Garanta. When a person needs their identity checked, BANXUM sends them to Didit. Didit runs the identity and anti-money-laundering checks and reports the result back. The default identity provider on every verification case is "didit".

sections.heading: 3. How money moves
body: Money flows in one big cycle. Follow it once and most screens will make sense.

Step 1, the investor sends a bank transfer. The investor wires money from their own bank to a Garanta collection bank account. "Collection account" just means the Garanta-controlled bank account that receives investor money.

Step 2, the transfer is matched and ledgered. When the money arrives, an admin confirms the bank operation and records it in the ledger (the system's official books), including the payer/source IBAN shown on the bank statement. The source IBAN must pass full checksum validation and then automatically becomes a verified payout account for that investor and currency. Crucially, the investor must also put a specific payment reference on their transfer so we can tell whose money it is. That reference has the exact format BX-{currency}-{investor_reference}, for example BX-CHF-AB12CD. The CHF deposit screen also shows a verified Swiss QR-bill code for Garanta_CHF, but that code identifies the collection account only; it does not replace the investor-specific BANXUM reference.

Step 3, the money becomes an investable balance. Once matched, the deposit creates a "balance lot" (think of it as a dated parcel of that investor's money) and the amount becomes investable. Balance buckets are explained in section 5.

Step 4, the investor invests in a loan (the primary market). The investor places an investment order against a published loan. Their investable balance is reserved for that loan. When the loan finishes funding, the reserved money is committed to it.
Step 5, the borrower is disbursed. Once a loan is fully funded and the borrower's KYB is approved, an admin pays out (disburses) the loan principal to the borrower's bank account.

Step 6, the borrower repays. Over the loan term the borrower sends money back to a Garanta collection account. Every payment follows one fixed order: Garanta legal costs/recovery fee, penalty, contractual interest, then principal. An admin records the evidence and amounts due; the server applies that order and distributes lender-facing amounts in proportion to current holdings.
Step 7, returns land back in the investor's balance. Each investor's share of principal and interest is credited back to their BANXUM balance as new balance lots.

Step 8, the investor withdraws to their bank. They can use a verified source account established by a deposit or request verification of another IBAN. An additional self-service request opens an admin finance task and remains unusable until reviewed. An admin then finalises the requested withdrawal after the bank transfer executes, or cancels it before execution.
bullets: Deposit reference format: BX-{currency}-{investor_reference}. It must appear, unchanged, in the bank transfer reference field, even when the investor uses the CHF QR-bill code.
Money only moves between real bank accounts at deposit (step 1-2), disbursement (step 5), repayment (step 6), and withdrawal (step 8). Everything in between is internal bookkeeping in the ledger.

Every money movement is recorded as a balanced double-entry journal in the ledger, and every confirmed bank transfer is recorded as a "bank operation". These records are append-only: they are never edited or deleted, only added to or reversed with a new entry.

sections.heading: 4. Money in BANXUM is not a bank account
body: This is the single most important idea for an operations admin. An investor's BANXUM balance is NOT a savings account.

The balance is non-interest-bearing operational money. "Non-interest-bearing" means simply holding money in BANXUM earns the investor nothing; interest only comes from funding loans. "Operational" means the balance exists so the investor can invest or withdraw, not to park cash. The funds are also segregated, meaning investor money is kept apart from Garanta's own money, not mixed with it.

Because BANXUM is not a deposit-taking bank, regulators do not allow investors to sit on idle cash indefinitely. So every balance lot is subject to ageing. Ageing means a parcel of money has clocks running against it from the day it was received, and what the investor is allowed to do with it changes as those clocks pass.
There are two ageing windows, measured from when the money was received:

Investment eligibility depends on the loan's remaining funding window, not a fixed day-30 cutoff. A 30-day remaining window needs at least 30 holding days left on every consumed source; a 10-day window needs 10. The final subscription date must precede the source's day-60 deadline. Funding windows contain at most 50 inclusive subscription dates. Eligible sources are consumed oldest-first.

The 60-day window (the withdrawal deadline). At 60 days the lot has reached the regulatory holding limit and must leave BANXUM. The investor cannot extend this deadline and neither can Garanta. The system sends the investor reminder emails as the deadline approaches (around days 25, 46, 53, 58, 59 and 60).

What happens when a lot reaches or passes the 60-day limit depends on whether the investor has given us a usable bank account to send the money to. "Usable" means a payout instruction (a registered IBAN) that an admin has verified. The handling fires on the first balance ageing scan at or after the deadline (the scan treats a lot as overdue once the business date is on or past the withdrawal deadline), so a lot already past 60 days is swept up too, not only one exactly on day 60. Two outcomes are possible, handled automatically by the balance ageing scan.
bullets: Forced withdrawal: if the investor HAS a verified, usable payout IBAN when a lot reaches or passes the 60-day limit, the system automatically creates a withdrawal request for that overdue money. "Forced" means the investor did not ask for it; the system raised it for them to honour the deadline. An admin then finalises the bank payout like any other withdrawal.

Penalty mode: if the investor has NO verified usable IBAN when a lot reaches or passes the 60-day limit, the system cannot send the money out, so the lot is moved into penalty mode. In plain words, a small daily charge starts eating into that specific balance (a per-day penalty in basis points, set as a deployment-level configuration value applied platform-wide; it is not a toggle you edit in the console). When any of the investor's money is in penalty mode, the investor app raises a blocking-severity "usable IBAN required" alert on their dashboard, prompting them to register a usable payout IBAN. Penalty-mode lots cannot be used for new investments, and the backend also blocks FX exchanges and secondary-market purchases while any penalty-mode balance exists. Withdrawal remains the intended exit path. If the daily charges ever consume the whole lot, it becomes penalty-exhausted (nothing left to charge).

Frozen: a separate balance lot status used when a lot is administratively held (for example during a compliance review). Frozen money still belongs to the investor but cannot be invested or withdrawn until the hold is lifted. Frozen is set deliberately, not by the ageing clock; penalty mode is what the 60-day clock produces when there is no usable IBAN.

sections.heading: 5. The balance buckets
body: When you look at an investor's money, it is grouped into buckets. A bucket is just a label describing what the investor can currently do with that money. The bucket is decided per balance lot, from the lot's status and its two ageing clocks. The same investor can have money in several buckets at once.

Only money that is genuinely still sitting in the balance (the "available" amount of a lot) counts toward these buckets; money already invested, withdrawn, converted in an FX exchange, or eaten by penalties does not.
bullets: investable: available money before its holding deadline. This is a potential amount: each loan's remaining funding window must fit within each consumed source's holding time. Shorter windows can use older funds.
withdraw-only: a compatibility bucket, normally zero under the current policy. There is no automatic day-30 investment ban. At day 60, uninvested funds instead enter the overdue return process.

overdue: available money past the 60-day withdrawal deadline. It is over the regulatory holding limit and must leave BANXUM. This is what the ageing scan turns into a forced withdrawal (if a usable IBAN exists) or penalty mode (if not).
frozen: money in a lot that has been administratively frozen. The investor can neither invest nor withdraw it until the freeze is removed.

penalty: money in a lot in penalty mode, being charged a daily penalty because it passed 60 days with no usable IBAN. Any penalty-mode balance raises a blocking-severity "usable IBAN required" alert in the investor app prompting them to fix their payout details. The penalty-mode lot itself is not investable, and current backend gates also block FX exchanges and secondary-market purchases until the situation is resolved. Withdrawal remains allowed so the money can leave the platform.
available (total): a roll-up of all of the above that still has money in it. It is the sum of every bucket; it is not a separate spendable pot of its own.

sections.heading: 6. The life of a loan
body: A loan moves through a fixed set of statuses. Knowing the order tells you what is and is not allowed at each step.
draft: the loan exists only as an internal record an admin is preparing. Investors cannot see it. It can still be edited freely.

published: an admin has published the loan to the marketplace, so investors can now see it and invest. A loan can only be published from draft, and only when its required fields, repayment schedule, funding window and the borrower's KYB gate all pass. Once published it has a published_at timestamp.

funded: enough investor money has been committed and an admin closes funding. Only a funded loan can be disbursed to the borrower. (Funding can also be cancelled before close, returning reserved money to investors; a never-funded loan can end up cancelled.)

performing vs late vs defaulted: after disbursement the borrower repays on a schedule. As long as installments are paid on time the loan keeps performing (its status stays funded). If an installment is overdue by 5 days or more the system marks the loan late. If an installment is overdue by 16 days or more it is marked defaulted.
repaid: the borrower has paid everything back. The loan is complete and investors have received their principal and interest.

defaulted then recovery or written-off: a defaulted loan moves into recovery, where Garanta tries to collect what it can (for example by enforcing collateral). Money recovered is distributed to investors. If nothing more can be collected, the remaining amount is written off, meaning it is formally recognised as a loss to the investors who funded it.
Primary market vs secondary market, in one line each:
bullets: Primary market: where loans are funded for the first time. An investor places an investment order on a published loan, their balance is reserved and allocated, and when funding closes the money is committed and the borrower is disbursed. This is the normal way money goes into a loan.

Secondary market: where an investor who already holds a piece of a loan resells that holding to another investor before the loan finishes, to get their money out early. The seller lists the holding (sometimes at a discount or premium); a buyer pays for it; Garanta takes a fee from each side. Some listings publish automatically and some need admin approval.

sections.heading: 7. Gates that protect everyone
body: BANXUM blocks risky or non-compliant actions by design. These blocks are called gates. The most important thing to understand: gates are enforced on the server (the backend), not just hidden in the screen. You cannot click your way past them in the admin console, and neither can an investor. If a gate is not satisfied, the action is refused server-side, full stop.
Identity gates. People are checked with KYC; companies are checked with KYB.

KYC (Know Your Customer) is identity and anti-money-laundering verification for a person, run through Didit. A KYC case has a status, and only one status, "approved", lets the person act. Every other status blocks them, including not_started, pending, declined, manual_review, high_risk, sanctions_hit, pep_hit, adverse_media_hit, expired, and reverification_required. A "sanctions hit" means the person matched a sanctions list; a "PEP hit" means they were flagged as a Politically Exposed Person (someone in or close to public office, who needs extra scrutiny). When Didit's automated result is unclear or flagged, the case goes to manual_review, where a Garanta compliance admin decides to approve, decline, or request re-verification. Company KYB is handled offline as described below.

Company KYB/AML is completed and retained by Garanta offline for borrowers, Loan Originators and legal-entity lenders. No platform company case or document pack is required. Explicit borrower compliance holds and Declined/Manual review decisions remain blocking. Missing, Pending or Expired optional records alone do not block transactions.
Phone verification. Sensitive money actions also require the investor's phone number to be verified. An account is phone-verified only once a verification challenge has been confirmed.

Account statuses. Every account carries a status: pending_kyc (the default for a brand-new account that has not finished verification), active, restricted, locked, or closed. Pending-KYC lender accounts may still log in so onboarding can resume, but they cannot use financial features yet. Restricted, locked, and closed accounts cannot log in; closing also makes the account inactive.

Putting it together for investors: the system only lets an investor reach financial features (balances, investing, withdrawing) when the account is an active lender AND the phone is verified. There is one more gate that depends on the account type. For a natural-person lender ("natural_person_lender"), that person must also have an approved KYC case. For a company representative ("legal_entity_lender_representative"), active-lender plus phone-verified is enough; there is no personal-KYC check on the representative, because Garanta completes company KYB offline; no stored company approval or documents are required. Miss a required gate and the financial screens are refused.
bullets: For natural-person lender KYC, only Approved permits financial access. Company KYB is offline; explicit restrictions remain enforceable.
Compliance hold overrides KYB: a borrower with approved KYB but an active compliance hold still cannot receive money.
Gates live in the backend. The console will not offer an override button, because the rule is enforced where the money actually moves.

sections.heading: 8. What the admin console is for
body: The console at /admin is organised into the main areas in the left-hand navigation. Here is each one in a single sentence so you know where to go.
bullets: Daily dashboard: your morning overview, showing the work queues that need attention today (KYC reviews, bank exceptions, withdrawals, forced withdrawals, balance ageing, funding loans, servicing, loan risk, secondary approvals, FX settlement, failed emails, reconciliation breaks).
Tasks: the admin task list, where operational to-dos are tracked and worked through.
Compliance: review natural-person lender KYC, manual-review cases and Didit risk flags. Company KYB is handled offline.

Finance ops: where money is handled, confirming deposits and bank operations, finalising withdrawals (including forced ones), running the balance ageing scan, handling FX (currency exchange) settlement, and doing reconciliation against the bank.
Loans: where you create and edit borrowers and loans, publish loans to the marketplace, and close or cancel funding.
Reports: where you generate operational and financial reports (for example FX delta and realised-settlement reports) for a chosen date range.
Users: where you search the full user directory, inspect account state, open read-only investor views, and apply audited account access controls.

Superadmin settings: superadmin-only configuration, such as document templates, platform settings and creating other admin accounts. QA mode is a separate staging/local section available to active regular admins as well.

sections.heading: 9. Staging, production, and QA fast-forwarding
body: BANXUM has separate deployment contexts. Production is the real customer environment at nxnarena.com. Staging is the private testing and training environment at staging.nxnarena.com. Staging runs the real application stack, not the browser-only preview fixtures, but it is still a test environment: data can be changed, reset, or rolled back during QA.

Preview mode, staging, and production are three different things. Preview mode is local/demo UI data and is marked as not real account data. Staging is a live backend/database used for private testing. Production is the real operating environment and should be treated as legal and operational truth.

QA mode is a staging/local-only admin feature for testing time-based behavior. Active regular admins and superadmins can open the separate QA mode section when the deployment allows it. Production hides these controls and rejects their API requests even for superadmins. Never use QA mode with real customer funds, real customer onboarding or live-money provider actions.

When QA mode is entered, the system captures a database snapshot. While QA mode is active, BANXUM's business-time helper returns the simulated time instead of normal wall-clock time. Advancing time is day-based: for each Europe/Zurich business date crossed, the system runs the daily jobs that would normally happen in real time.

Fast-forwarding is intended to behave like real time for core platform jobs. It runs balance ageing and penalty charging, servicing status scans, primary funding-deadline resolution, reconciliation-break task sync, Loan Originator settlement-task sync, originator lifecycle scans and due email dispatch for the crossed dates. This lets admins test funding-window/day-60 balance behavior, forced withdrawals, penalty mode, late/default transitions, campaign expiry, automatic LO activation at funding close and scheduled notifications without waiting weeks.

Restore seed returns to the original regression seed, including its original simulated clock, accounts and balances. Create snapshot saves a later checkpoint without replacing that seed; Restore snapshot returns to this checkpoint. Without a manually saved snapshot, seed is the default and Restore snapshot is disabled. Records created after the selected restore point disappear. The restoring admin receives a fresh session if the restored credentials and permissions still match; all other sessions must sign in again.
bullets: Use staging QA mode only for private testing, training, and regression checks. Do not use it to create legal production evidence or operate real money.

Snapshot/revert covers database state, not already-sent email/SMS, downloaded files, object-storage artifacts or other external side effects. Restore checks the snapshot checksum and migration signature before an atomic flush/load; failure leaves the previous database intact. After schema migrations, the environment owner must upgrade the saved baseline in an isolated database or explicitly create a new seed; never bypass these checks.

QA snapshot, restore and fast-forward take an exclusive environment lock. Concurrent application requests and scheduled jobs are refused temporarily. Fast-forward runs the relevant jobs for crossed dates. Do not run uncoordinated database scripts during QA operations.

Coordinate with other testers, save evidence outside the database, then restore the seed between independent regression branches. Use Restore snapshot only when intentionally resuming that saved checkpoint.

sections.heading: 10. Loan Originators: funding and activating an existing claim
body: A Loan Originator is a professional lender that already owns loans to final business borrowers. It can offer part of a performing loan through a finite BANXUM subscription round. Investor money is reserved during funding; it does not immediately become a holding or start earning interest.

Company KYB is completed and retained by Garanta offline; platform compliance files are optional. The final borrower's legal name is private unless an admin explicitly publishes it for that loan. Otherwise investors see its public display name. The originator has no BANXUM login or wallet; an internal payable tracks external transfers.

The underlying coupon is what the final borrower pays. The admin separately declares what percentage of attributable interest and penalty belongs to investors. Principal is subscribed at par: one currency unit of cash buys one unit of outstanding principal at activation. The displayed Yield is a nominal participating-coupon indicator, not a guaranteed effective return.

At full subscription, or after the funding deadline with any positive subscription, BANXUM closes the round and immediately creates active holdings and originator payable in one transaction. No separate activation action or borrower receipt is required. The boundary installment belongs entirely to the LO. Investor principal, interest and penalty rights follow the original published schedule after that boundary.

A processing failure preserves reservations, hides the opportunity and raises an urgent task plus operations email. Repair its cause promptly; automatic retries retain the published funding outcome. An admin cannot cancel a subscribed expired or failed round instead. A change discovered while funding is still open requires cancellation and a replacement opportunity before the deadline. Missing borrower payments after activation follow servicing, not an activation waiting stage. Incompatible legacy closed records raise a repair task without invented payment evidence.

Activation creates originator payable rather than borrower disbursement. Finance Operations settles accumulated activation and servicing payables in complete batches. A task appears when the oldest amount is three days old and settlement must occur no later than day five. There is no originator buyback or recourse guarantee.
bullets: Use only the Loan Originator close, cancellation and repayment actions. Activation is automatic at close. Do not use direct-loan disbursement or direct servicing for LO claims.
Do not publish from an unverified spreadsheet. Reconcile the full CSV to the legal contract, originator servicing export and bank evidence.
Do not change the CSV simply to make validation pass. Put the opportunity on hold and investigate discrepancies.
New refinancing-loan creation is disabled. Existing legacy refinancing loans remain readable and serviceable; Loan Originator claims are the new product for purchasing an existing loan claim.

Only performing originator holdings are resellable in v1. Current holdings may be listed only at par or a discount; premiums are rejected. Private acquisition economics are never shown to a secondary buyer.
